raw_response:
I am old now, 65, and I have been doing wheat and maize for 50 years on this ground in Quzhou. I know this land. My 10.1 mu is not small, not big — enough to feed us and sell some. Two of us at home, me and my wife, so we cannot do everything by hand like before. I hire the combine for wheat harvest and the seeder.

Last year's wheat gave me around 500 kg per mu, maize around 600 kg. Not bad, not the best. My neighbor Old Wang got a bit more but he uses more fertilizer. I do what has worked.

For wheat, I will plant Jimai variety like last year — the seed shop sells it, most people here use it. I put down compound fertilizer before ploughing, about 2 bags (100 jin, 50 kg) of 15-15-15 per mu as base, then top-dress with urea (about half a bag, 25 jin, 12-13 kg) at green-up in spring. That gives me maybe 25 kg of pure nitrogen counting everything. Phosphorus and potassium from the compound, about 7-8 kg each. I plough in autumn before wheat — deeper is better for the roots to hold through winter. Water: once before winter to seal in, once at jointing, once at heading if dry. Three times. Spray once for aphids and once for weeds in spring, sometimes a fungicide if I see rust — call it three sprays.

For maize, after wheat harvest I do no-till direct seeding — everyone does now, saves time and the stalks stay for mulch. Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid, whatever the dealer has fresh. Base fertilizer less than wheat, about 1.5 bags compound per mu, then urea top-dress at big trumpet stage, maybe 15 kg urea. Total N about 20 kg. Water twice if the rains come, three times if dry summer. Spray once for borer, once for weeds — two sprays usually enough.

I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than come up short. Fertilizer costs money but a bad harvest costs much more. I do not change much year to year — change is risky at my age.
